title: REMEMBER WHAT YOUR EYES HAVE SEEN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the terms of the covenant the Lord commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Horeb. Moses summoned all the Israelites and said to them: Your eyes have seen all that the Lord did in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials and to all his land." — Deut 29:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel stood on the edge of the promised land, Moses called them to remember. Before laying out the renewed covenant, he pointed back to what their own eyes had seen — the mighty things God did in Egypt, the plagues, the deliverance, Pharaoh humbled. He wanted their obedience to be rooted in memory: this is the God who rescued you.

Memory is a powerful anchor for faith. When we forget what God has done, we drift into fear and doubt. But when we deliberately remember His past faithfulness — how He provided, how He carried us through, how He answered when we cried out — our trust for the future grows stronger. Faith often feeds on memory.

This is why Moses keeps saying, "Your eyes have seen." He was not asking them to believe in a distant, theoretical God, but in the God who had proven Himself before their very eyes.

We have seen God's greatest act of rescue too — not with physical eyes, but through the testimony of Scripture. At the cross, God delivered us from a bondage far greater than Egypt. Jesus told us to remember His death with bread and cup, "in remembrance of me" (Luke 22:19). When your faith feels shaky, look back. Remember the cross. Remember His faithfulness in your own story. The God who has already done so much will not fail you now.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last deliberately remember what God has done for me?
2. How does recalling God's past faithfulness strengthen my trust today?
3. What "rescue" in my life do I need to remember afresh?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me remember all You have done. When my faith grows weak, anchor me in the memory of Your faithfulness, and above all in the cross of Christ. Amen.
